status.en: 9 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 50% more than the week before, most of them in Juba, Rumbek and Akobo.
status.nb: 9 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 50 prosent flere enn uken før, flest i Juba, Rumbek og Akobo.

summary.en: Violence continues in South Sudan with a grenade explosion that killed four children and injured two in Northern Bahr el Ghazal, and clashes between Warrap and Lakes communities that left 14 dead. The government dispatched 25 young professionals to Brazil for specialized farming training and President Salva Kiir traveled to Ethiopia. UNHCR and South Sudan officials held talks to improve support for refugees in Egypt. Four individuals received 14-year prison sentences for a sexual assault case in Sherikat. The UCDP recorded two battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Vold fortsetter i Sør-Sudan med en granateksplosjon som drepte fire barn og såret to i Nord-Bahr el Ghazal, og sammenstøt mellom Warrap‑ og Lakes-samfunn som førte til 14 døde. Regjeringen sendte 25 unge fagfolk til Brasil for spesialisert jordbrukstrening, og president Salva Kiir reiste til Etiopia. UNHCR og sør-sudanske myndigheter holdt samtaler om bedre støtte til flyktninger i Egypt. Fire personer fikk 14‑årige fengselsstraffer for en seksuell overgrepssak i Sherikat. UCDP registrerte to dødsfall i kamp i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
